tolerance.basis: BET is the same qsm-core source compiled to WebAssembly in the browser bundle and the command line, and WebAssembly arithmetic is deterministic. The command line reproduced this mask bit for bit, so any difference is a defect.

The native command line reproduced this mask bit for bit on linux-x64 and macos-arm64 (PR #198), as did ONNX Runtime Web under Node. Other CPUs' kernels can round differently and move boundary voxels; SYNcro's native SynthStrip pipeline kept brain-mask Dice 0.9999987 against its reference (packages/syncro/validation/README.md). Dice 0.99995 allows about 160 of the 1.6 million mask voxels to differ.

The same runtime, pipeline and tolerance as synthstrip, with FreeSurfer's no-CSF weights. The command line reproduced this mask bit for bit on linux-x64, and it differs from mri_synthstrip --no-csf (freesurfer/synthstrip@sha256:ebbc1772) in 2 of its 1.4 million voxels.

The command line runs @brainchop/mindgrab 0.1.20260925's CPU modules, the WebAssembly this browser run used, through @neurodesk/node-drivers/mindgrab, whose outputs match Chromium's byte for byte on Linux, Windows and macOS (packages/node-drivers/validation/reference.json). Any difference is a defect.
